title: Outreach
sections: Outreach

COVID Microgrant Program: We launched a microgrant program to provide $500 to one returning LA/SoCal FTC team that has been affected by COVID-19. In particular, we strove to create an inclusive community by giving special consideration to teams with more students from underserved, underrepresented, and vulnerable populations who have been disproportionately harmed by the pandemic.

LA FTC Webinar: Our team spoke at a SoCal FTC webinar about team interaction and management in a pandemic. We talked about three main aspects of working online—courage, or the ability to form bonds and try new things; connection, or ways to stay close as a team even if you can’t all see each other in person with technology and scheduling tips; and collaboration, with details about the methods and tools we have used to work well together virtually. We call these the 3 C’s of Curiosity.

Wolf Corp Showcase: As a member of the winning alliance at Regionals last season, we were invited to speak at a showcase held by FTC team #12525 Wolf Corp. We shared advice about our design process and spoke about the insights that we have learned over the years about how to succeed in FTC.

ONSHAPE Webinar: We were invited to present at a webinar hosted by PTC about how we use Onshape in FTC. We answered live questions and gave advice, tips, and tricks that we have learned over the years. This webinar has since been viewed hundreds of times!

Guide to Github: Our programming team made an in-depth video and instruction manual for teams looking to get involved with Github. Click here to check it out!

FIRST Like a Girl Ambassador: As a FIRST Like a Girl ambassador, we collaborate with other teams to post and share what girls, especially we as a girls’ team, can do in FIRST. We primarily do this through our Instagram and Twitter accounts, which combined have over 1,300 followers. In addition, we promote events and opportunities for women to be involved in FIRST and STEM as a whole.

Shanghai International Youth Tech Expo: We created a video for and presented our Skystone robot at the Shanghai International Youth Technology Expo. We shared about FTC, last year’s game, our design process, and the mechanisms and construction of our final robot.

title: Robot
sections:
ROBOT: Katherine droneson

The name of our robot is a play on the name of Katherine Johnson, an African-American woman who did trajectory analysis for NASA during America's first human spaceflight in 1961 and helped calculate the Apollo 11 moon landing. By naming our robot after Ms. Johnson, we seek to inspire and empower our team members to embrace challenges in the male-dominated field of robotics with the same tenacity and brilliance that defined Katherine Johnson’s career.

Intake: Three levels of active wheels (boot and kick-up wheels)

Lift: Misumi Slides and custom-made pulleys

Scoring: Custom CNCed polycarbonate box with mini servos, mounted on a custom aluminum CNCed arm

Drivetrain: Four wheel goBilda Mecanum Drive with Vertically Mounted Motors

Drone: Compresed string is propelled using a servo, all mounted on another servo

Wire Management: Slinky (not pictured)

title: 2023 - 24 Season
sections: Our eighth season of FTC is complete, and we are so grateful to all of the mentors, referees, and volunteers who have been apart of our CenterStage season! This season, we welcomed twelve new members who were able to learn and grow skills surrounding CAD, fabrication tools such as the laser cutter, 3D printer, and CNC machine, and a mix of hardware and software skills. We've become great friends and teammates over this season, and used each of our unique skills to build an innovative robot! In order to work towards our goal of truly embodying FIRST's mission of connecting with our community, we have taught with organizations such as Alexandria House and Mar Vista Family Center. We were also able to start and fund an FLL team at Boys and Girls Club Los Angeles and teach lessons at the Center for Early Education. We've been lucky to connect with tons of other FTC teams and gain valuable mentorship and advice from professionals in STEM from organizations such as JPL, Aerospace, NASA, Northrop Grumman, and more! Lastly, we were able to take home first place Inspire at Regionals and first place Think at Worlds! Overall, we've had an amazing season and we feel extremely grateful for everyone who has helped us!

title: Robot
sections:
ROBOT: ROSALIND PLANKTON

Our robot is named after Rosalind Franklin, an English chemist known for discovering the helical structure of DNA and virus structure. By naming our robot after Ms. Franklin, we seek to inspire and empower our team members to embrace challenges and think outside the box. Similarly, we hope our team will embrace principles of discovery and innovation that defined Franklin’s career in a male-dominated field. By combining these values with a sea-themed pun for Curiosity flair, we got our robot name!

Intake: We have an active intake with kickup wheels and surgical tubing connected to a pivot point

Lift: Misumi Slides and custom-made pulleys

Drivetrain: For our drivetrain, we utilize a four-wheel mecanum direct drive with two odometry pods and one GoBilda Pinpoint odometry computer for localization. We designed a clear polycarbonate bottom panel along with a custom CNC’d and pocketed aluminum panels to ensure visibility and screw accessibility.

Linkage: For our extension mechanism, we chose a two-armed, servo-powered linkage with three stages of Misumi linear slides. 

Scoring: Since our goal was to cycle without rotating, our pivot has a 350 degree range of motion to allow the claw to grab samples from the intake on one, and take specimens off the wall on the opposite side

Wire Management: Slinky (not pictured)

title: About Us
sections: About Us

Who We Are

We are Curiosity, a FIRST Tech Challenge team from Marlborough School in Los Angeles, California. Our mission is to set an example for aspiring young scientists and to demonstrate what young women can accomplish in the world of STEM. We strive to do so by competing in FTC, which allows us to continue to grow and learn alongside our teammates, mentors, and other inventive thinkers in our community. 

We prioritize bringing new and unique ideas into the world, whether that be through our creation of custom parts or our distinctive outreach events.  Above all, we believe it is essential to adhere to our core values of innovation, positivity, diligence, and, of course, curiosity.

title: Blog
sections: Blog

kickoff | 9/7/24

Curiosity traveled to Monrovia today for the Into the Deep Season kickoff! We had an amazing time seeing the new game, and we also presented two portfolio workshops to over 150 people. We also made an appearance in the game video (SO EXCITING!!!) and started considering strategy and early design ideas for this years' game in a three hour work session. While we were slightly sad there was no live fish in the game, the climbing during endgame and the clip/human player interaction seem exciting! We can't wait to dive into this season!

BACK TO SCHOOL (AND THIS BLOG) | 8/29/24

Hi Everyone! We know it's been a while (some may say a long while) but we are back and better than ever! We had a lot going on last season, including 12 new team members, but we are back to this blog! We've spent our offseason planning out outreach, including our FLL team, keeping up our connections with STEM professionals, portfolio feedbacks, and some new, extensive outreach as well. We've also started planning out our season and team structure. Keep an eye out for more updates!

Regional Championship | 3/11/23

Curiosity had an amazing time at regionals and are elated to announce our qualification for the World Championships in Houston! We went undefeated in our qualifying matches and entered alliance selection as the first seed. We were unfortunately eliminated in semifinals. Thank you to our alliance partners Pineapple Something 20824 and Alpha Genesis 6436! Despite our defeat in semifinals, we stayed hopeful and won 1st place Inspire Award as well as 2nd place Promote Award. We are thrilled to be advancing to World Championships along with two other Southern California teams, Blueprints 7767 and GatorBytes 18457!

Inter-league tournament | 2/26/23

ILT was a major success for Team Curiosity! We had a great time connecting with the rest of our league and competing for the six advancement slots. We went undefeated in our qualifying matches and were winning alliance captain. A special thank you to our alliance partners Alpha Genesis 6436 and Marlbots 3526! We also won 3rd place Inspire Award, 3rd place Think Award, and 1st place Connect Award.

Regionals | 3/12/22

Curiosity had a wonderful time competing, socializing, and dancing at Regionals! It was great to see all the hardworking teams in action. We are grateful to have won 3rd place Inspire and 1st place Think! A huge thank you to our alliance partners 16321 X Drive and 3526 Marlbots! Congratulations to all teams, and we will see everyone next season!

qualifiers | 2/20/22

Curiosity had a great time at Qualifiers! We are grateful to have won 1st place Think and 2nd place Inspire! Congrats to all teams! Special thank you to our alliance partners in the semifinals: 5390 Vikings and Rock N Roll Robots 25! We can’t wait for Regionals and we will see you guys there!

Meet 3 | 1/22/22

We had such a great time at Meet 3 on Saturday, and we are so proud of all of the teams in A1! Seeing all of the progress you guys have made on your robots from Meet 0 to now is so inspiring! Special thanks to all the referees, mentors, and volunteers that helped all of the meets go smoothly- we appreciate everything that you do for us!

Curiosity is also grateful to be named League Champion for SoCal League A1! We can’t wait to attend the Qualifier in February! 

Watch Meet 3 here!

Meet 2 | 12/18/21

Curiosity had an amazing time at Meet 2! We loved seeing all of the progress that teams have made to their robots, and we can’t wait to see everyone again at Meet 3. Thank you to our mentors, all of the people who volunteered, and all of the teams that competed!

You can watch Meet 2 here!

Meet 1 | 12/4/21

Curiosity had a great time at Meet 1! Thank you to all of the teams that competed and special thanks to our alliance partners. All team members had a great time collaborating in preparation and it was great to see everyone in person after a year online. Thank you to our mentors Mr. Witman and Dr. Mirsky for aiding us throughout the process. We can't wait for Meet 2!

You can watch Meet 1 here!

KICKOFF | 9/18/21

The season has begun again! We gave an awesome presentation about our portfolio from last year at Kickoff for the 21-22 season (you can see it in the resources tab). We've gained several new members this year and we're super excited to start up again this season! You can expect more updates to the website soon!

Championships | 4/25/21

Yesterday, we competed in the LAFTC Championships! We were so proud of the progress we had made on the robot since the qualifying tournament. Our highest score was 201 points, a team record. We won first place Think, third place Connect, and second place Compass for our amazing mentor, Mr. Witman. Congratulations to all the teams who competed! We had so much fun and it was an incredible day.

Championship UPDATES | 4/19/21

We're working hard preparing for Regionals on 4/24! Other than updating our engineering notebook, portfolio, and judging, we are making some upgrades to the robot. First, we added on "ring wands" to block the rings from getting past our bot in Tele-Op. This doubles as a driver controlled enhancement! Next, we increased the speed of our auto with the goal to be able to pick up a second wobble goal. We hope to get that done before next week's competition!

Qualifying tournament | 4/3/21

We had a fantastic time at our qualifying tournament on 4/3/2021! We are grateful to have placed 1st in robot performance, won the 2nd place Inspire Award, won the 1st place Think Award, and won the 2nd place Control Award. We are also excited that one of our mentors, Mr. Witman, won the 2nd place Compass Award. We are so excited to compete at regionals! Congratulations to all of the teams that competed!

title: Community Partners
sections: Community Partners

Supporting women in STEM

What is #FIRSTLikeAGirl?

A social media movement to encourage girls and women in STEM and FIRST. By showcasing the many incredible women of FIRST and their stories, girls can find role models who they identify with and are inspired by.

Why is this important?

Through this social media campaign, we empower girls with the confidence to overcome cultural pressures, follow their dreams in STEM, and become active members of the FIRST community.

Get Involved!

Create a video, sponsor our buttons, encourage young women and girls to pursue STEM, join or mentor a FIRST team or volunteer for one of the more than 2,600 FIRST events in your community. Be a part of the solution, be a part of the FIRST community!

FIRST#LikeAGirl is an initiative started by FRC 1902 Exploding Bacon.

title: Curiosity Cares

Team Curiosity is on a mission to recycle as many FTC game elements as possible by reclaiming their plastic and keeping them out of landfills. We’re currently accepting donations of retired field elements from teams worldwide.

📍If you're located near Los Angeles [SoCal or LAUSD Region], we’re happy to drive out and pick them up—no matter the quantity.

title: Team Curiosity 11770
sections: Curiosity - FTC #11770
Inspired by our namesake, the Curiosity Mars rover, we believe in making an impact through exploration, innovation, and above all, collaboration.

Purpose

We are a robotics team of girls and gender minorities from Marlborough School in Los Angeles. We have participated in FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC) since 2016. Our mission is to set an example for aspiring young scientists and to demonstrate what young women can accomplish in the world of STEM.
Courage · Connection · Collaboration

title: 2016-17 Season
sections: 2016-17 Season: Velocity vortex

2016-17 was Curiosity's first season competing in FTC. Despite this being our rookie year, we ended up ranking first in our league before our Inter-League Tournament (ILT). At our ILT, we won the 3rd place Think Award for our detailed and clear engineering notebook.

title: 2017-18 Season
sections: 2017-18 Season: relic recovery

After an amazing rookie year, we participated in FTC during the 2017-18 season. We were part of the winning alliance at our ILT, helping us qualify for the Los Angeles Regional Championship for the first time.

title: 2018-19 Season
sections: 2018-19 Season: Rover ruckus

Rover Ruckus was our third season participating in FTC. During this season, we started utilizing our school’s laser cutter and 3D printer more often, allowing us to design and fabricate custom parts that helped set our robot above the rest. Along with a slew of other awards, we won the 1st place Judges Award at our ILT, an award chosen by the tournament’s judges to represent our unique efforts, performance, and team dynamics. At the end of this season, our main outreach effort was a project to create wheelchairs for dogs. We used a Computer-Aided Design (CAD) program called Onshape to create custom-fitted wheelchairs for dogs.

title: Portfolio Support
sections: Portfolio Support

Team Curiosity 11770 has won the Think Award many times, and even at the World Championship level. Because of this, we consider ourselves experts in building and editing a portfolio, and would love to extend that expertise to help you and your team succeed! We have two options of portfolio support and editing - please pick the one that works best for your team below! Additionally, we give portfolio presentations at season kickoffs and at other various events year. Recordings of those can be seen on the resources page.

feedback (2-8 PAGE DOCUMENT WITH SUGGESTIONS/EDITS)

In this option, we will review your portfolio and send back a document with listed edits and suggestions. Please submit your portfolio to submit your portfolio here as a complete draft. Please only upload a PDF; we will not be able to provide feedback if it is in other formats. Additionally, upload any specific questions or areas you would like specific advice on. We will do our best to get edits to you within a week (usually we're pretty fast!); if we expect to take longer, we'll email you to let you know.

dIRECT SUPPORT FROM CURIOSITY (ONLINE MEETING + FEEDBACK)

In our direct option, please set up a meeting with us at schedule a meeting here. We will meet for roughly thirty minutes on Google Meet, depending on how long it takes and how far you are into developing your portfolio, and go through every page and section providing feedback and edits. 

Bring:

Your portfolio (online please, so you can share your screen if need be)

Email your portfolio to us beforehand (team11770@marlborough.org) - please do this ASAP

Team members who both are working on the portfolio and are knowledgeable to some extent about your technical and non-technical work

A way to take down notes/feedback (we will send you a copy of our own feedback, but just in case you want your own notes)

We contributed to T.W.C.A.'s portfolio resource! Check out T.W.C.A.’s portfolio resource.

If you are looking for portfolio examples, we have past portfolios in the North Star section of Constellation.
